cards.explanation: The crowds are amazed, just like the verse says. A man who couldn't speak is suddenly talking, and I'd have dropped a whole tray of cookies on the spot. Hold on to that amazement, friends. The next verse shows it didn't land the same way for everybody.

They call Beelzebul the prince of the demons. So some people watched a man get his voice back and said the power behind it was the ruler of demons. Friends, that is a WILD thing to say. Jesus is about to answer them.
The word is sign. Others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven. A man had just started talking, and they asked for something on top of that. The text calls it testing, friends.

Jesus says every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste. He adds that a house divided against a house will fall. Picture two people yanking one cookie sheet in opposite directions. Nobody gets cookies, friends, just a floor full of crumbs.

The answer is their judges. Jesus says, "And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges." He asks about their own sons, and then names those sons as the judges. I'd say that's a smooth move.

The word is kingdom. Jesus says if He drives out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon them. He's answering the accusation head on. That's a lot to say about one man who just started talking.

Jesus says someone stronger attacks and overpowers the strong man, and takes away the armor he trusted. Then he divides up the plunder. The fully armed man had everything lined up, and it still wasn't enough against someone stronger.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.” There's no standing in the middle here. Either you're gathering with Him or you're scattering.
The word is house. The spirit passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, "I will return to the house I left." So it heads back to the place it came from.

Jesus says the spirit brings seven spirits more wicked than itself. They go in and dwell there. The house was swept clean and put in order, and still it gets new tenants, and these are more wicked than the first. Jesus says, "And the final plight of that man is worse than the first."
The answer is False. Jesus says, "And the final plight of that man is worse than the first." It's a heavy line, so I'll just say it plainly. The man doesn't end up better off.

Jesus says those who hear the word of God and obey it are blessed. He replies, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.” A woman in the crowd lifted her voice with a blessing, and He pointed to hearing and obeying. That's the one to take home with you, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). So He's talking about Himself when He says the Son of Man will be a sign.

The word is greater. Jesus says, “…now One greater than Solomon is here.” The Queen of the South came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. Jesus is saying someone even greater is here now.

The answer is False. Jesus says the Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them. She came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. Now One greater than Solomon is here.

The reason Jesus gives is that they repented at the preaching of Jonah. The men of Nineveh did that, and now One greater than Jonah is here. Nineveh listened to Jonah's preaching, and Jesus says someone greater is here now.

The reason Jesus gives is so those who enter can see the light. A lamp goes on a stand for that very purpose. A lamp has a job, and hiding it in a cellar defeats the whole point. It's like baking a fresh batch and hiding the tray in a closet while the guests wait.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light." He goes on to say that when they are bad, the body is full of darkness. So the eye is like the lamp for the whole body.

The word is darkness. Jesus says, "Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness." It's a warning to check on the light. I sat for years in the back of a dark junk drawer, so I'll tell you, friends, I'd rather have the light on.

Jesus says you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you. That's for the one whose whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness. It's a picture of being lit up from head to toe. No dark corners anywhere.
